# Model Zoo

OLM implements 27 model families from 14 organisations as readable PyTorch, with 47 named presets that follow the published architecture of a released model. Every number on this page is generated from the code: each preset is built on PyTorch's `meta` device and its parameters are counted, so the tables describe what OLM actually builds.

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_model_zoo.py from the code in src/olm/models. Do not edit by hand: run `PYTHONPATH=src python scripts/gen_model_zoo.py`. -->

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Presets are architectures, not checkpoints.** A preset such as `Llama3_1_8B()` builds the released model's architecture with **randomly initialised weights**. OLM does not download or load pretrained weights. Use a preset to train from scratch, to study or ablate the architecture, or to check shapes and parameter counts on the `meta` device.

```python
import torch
from olm.models import Llama3_2_1B

with torch.device("meta"):  # shapes only: no memory, no weights
    model = Llama3_2_1B()
print(f"{sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters()):,}")
```

Annotated architecture guides walk through the source of [Qwen3 MoE](qwen-3.md), [DeepSeek-V3](deepseek-v3.md), [Gemma 3](gemma-3.md), [Llama 3.1 / 3.2](llama-3.md), [Kimi K2 and Kimi Linear](kimi.md), [GPT-2](gpt-2.md): what changed from the previous generation, the code section by section, and a tiny model you can train on a CPU.

## Preset sizes

*Total* counts every parameter once (a tied output head shares the embedding matrix). *Active* is reported for mixture-of-experts models: the parameters one token passes through, that is the total minus the routed experts it is not sent to and minus any multi-token-prediction head.

† Includes the multi-token-prediction (MTP) head, an auxiliary training module that the default `forward` does not use.

## Layer mix

The token mixers (attention and its linear-time alternatives) and feed-forward layers each preset builds, counted per layer. Attention entries read `query heads/key-value heads`; MLA and the linear-time mixers give their head count alone (`MLA 128h`); sliding-window entries give the window in tokens; `MoE 256e top-8 +1 shared` is 256 routed experts of which each token uses 8, plus one expert every token uses.

## How this page is made

[`scripts/gen_model_zoo.py`](https://github.com/openlanguagemodel/openlanguagemodel/blob/main/scripts/gen_model_zoo.py) imports `olm.models`, treats every class whose `__init__` takes no arguments as a preset of the base class it inherits from, and builds each preset under `torch.device("meta")`. It writes this page and [`zoo.json`](https://github.com/openlanguagemodel/openlanguagemodel/blob/main/docs/models/zoo.json), which also holds every preset's resolved constructor arguments and the `Structure:` section of each family's docstring. The website's model pages read the same JSON.

Parameter counts describe OLM's implementation. Where OLM builds a released architecture differently (for example, a preset that ties the output head to the embedding when the release does not), the count follows the code. Each architecture guide ends with the differences it found for its family.

After adding or changing a model family, regenerate the page from the repository root:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python scripts/gen_model_zoo.py
```
